messages.subject: RNG News
parts:
I came across this new RNG that claims to offer lots of the features
we require (http://www.pcg-random.org/paper.html) and includes a
thorough testing of it along with a bunch of existing RNGs
(http://www.pcg-random.org/paper.html).

The paper is pretty informal (quotes Douglas Adams at one point)
but the tests look impressive and the code is available as
header-only C++ (supposedly to match the C++11 random
library API). Interestingly the (L’)Ecuyer generator from boost
that we currently use seems to be one of the best competitors
to this new algorithm so we’re not doing too badly...
